met_analysis:
The Low Pressure Area over Coastal areas of south Odisha - north Andhra Pradesh lies over South Chhattisgarh & neighbourhood at 0530 hrs IST of today, the 12th September 2026. The associated cyclonic circulation extends upto 9.4 km above mean sea level tilting southwestwards with height. It is likely to move west-northwestwards across south Chhattisgarh & Vidarbha during next 24 hours.
The Monsoon trough at mean sea level now passes through Jaisalmer, Kota, Bhopal, Nagpur, centre of Low Pressure Area over south Chhattisgarh & neighbourhood and thence east southeastwards to Eastcentral Bay of Bengal and extends upto 1.5 km above mean sea level.
The trough from north Rajasthan to cyclonic circulation associated with the Low Pressure Area over south Chhattisgarh & neighbourhood across Madhya Pradesh & Chhattisgarh extending upto 3.1 km above mean sea level has merged with monsoon trough.
The trough from South Interior Karnataka to Gulf of Mannar across Tamil Nadu at 0.9 km above mean sea level persists.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over south Konkan off Eastcentral Arabian sea persists and now seen between 3.1 & 7.6 km above mean sea level titling southwestwards with height.
The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over north Punjab & neighbourhood now lies over north Pakistan & adjoining Jammu between 3.1 & 4.5 km above mean sea level with a trough aloft in middle tropospheric westerlies level with its axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level runs roughly along Long. 70°E to the north of Lat. 30°N
